text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — POP us-east-1 (edge POP ID: pop-use1-04) showing sustained packet loss >25% p95 on egress to CDN peers. Impact: increased latency and partial failures for streaming and websocket traffic. Alert rule: cdn.edge.packet_loss > 20% for 5m. https://ops.redwood/alerts/1825001234

maria: i'm on pager, checking BGP & traceroutes to that POP now. grabbing peers list and recent config changes.

Devin: saw a bunch of BGP flaps from Provider-Prime in the last 10m, AS64512 peers toggling. mtr -> next-hop shows alternating high loss at provider hop.

maria: copying outputs below:
```
# mtr -r -c 50 pop-use1-04 -> 34.200.12.45
 1.|-- 10.0.1.1   0.0%  0.2ms
 2.|-- 203.0.113.5  0.0%  1.1ms
 3.|-- 198.51.100.7 32.0% 24.3ms  <-- packetloss spike
 4.|-- 34.200.12.45 27.0% 30.2ms
```

maria: netops-vendor, can you confirm any maintenance or upstream issues on Provider-Prime?

netops-vendor: Provider-Prime reported an interface flapping on their peering router at 20:06 UTC, ticket TP-9981 opened. They're rerouting internally but some routes are oscillating. We're pushing to them to stabilize, ETA unknown.

Sanjay: scope of impact? Which customers/regions hit hardest?

Jess: support triage — preliminary telemetry: ~12% of active sessions saw reconnects in US-EAST between 20:00-20:10 UTC. Top affected product: live-stream ingestion (customers: AcmeMedia, Streamly). Notifying customer ops now.

Kyle: quick mitigation idea: route-around by shifting traffic from pop-use1-04 to pop-use1-06 and pop-use2-01 via steering rules. Can we change CDN edge routing map?

Devin: yes, we can adjust steering. two options:
1) Soft fail traffic away from pop-use1-04 for new sessions (preferential route to pop-use1-06)
2) Emergency global redirect for websocket/upstream to fallback POPs (higher latency but stable)
I can apply (1) now, will take ~45s to propagate to edge controllers.

maria: do (1) now. also enable prefix-bypass for origin-to-edge so ingestion doesn't stall. document commands:
```
# edge-control steer set --pop pop-use1-04 --weight 0 --reason "provider flapping"
# edge-control steer set --pop pop-use1-06 --weight 100
```

maria: applying steer. watch metrics.

incident-bot: Change applied by Devin at 20:12:08 UTC: steer weights updated.

Devin: metrics already trending down for packet loss on CDN aggregator. p95 loss dropped to ~6% after steering. websocket errors from 12% -> 2.1% in 3m.

Jess: ping to customers: "We've routed traffic away from an affected edge POP in us-east; ingestion should be restored. We're investigating root cause with our upstream provider and will share updates." Will post to status.redwood.com.

netops-vendor: Provider-Prime continues to confirm packet loss on a distribution interface. They're planning a full failover to alternate fabric; estimated stabilization in 30-45m.

Sanjay: plan for handoff: Maria, can you do a 30m check and then hand to me if still open? Also set escalation if regression occurs.

maria: yes. i'll monitor for 30m. leaving notes in incident channel. handing to Sanjay at 20:45 UTC if stable.

Kyle: creating incident incident-triage doc in /incidents/1825001234 (internal) with timeline and mitigation commands.

Jess: updating status page and posting a targeted message to impacted customers. adding ticket numbers for escalation.

Devin: follow-up actions: request BGP dump from Provider-Prime, capture peering logs, and run replay on our edge sim to see if config interacted with flap.

maria: adding runbook checklist: monitor edge packet loss, watch long tail reconnects, validate origin-to-edge caches, confirm provider ticket TP-9981 resolution.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation in place — traffic steered off pop-use1-04. Continue monitoring. If packet loss resurfaces or steering doesn't hold, escalate to network incident (sev2) and page the on-call network lead.

Sanjay: thanks team. i'll take it at 20:45 if still open. Jess, keep customers updated every 30m until resolved.

Jess: will do. posting first customer outbound now. :thumbsup:

maria: leaving a quick note for postmortem: consider automatic steering threshold lowering and add a validation to catch route-oscillation loops that prevent steering from sticking.

Devin: added a follow-up ticket for edge-controller sticky checks.

netops-vendor: we'll update when Provider-Prime confirms failover completion.

maria: ending active push. monitoring-only. will hand off per plan.
